title: Localization of an internal finite basis with its specified scalar map
statement:
Let $C$ be a small site whose abelian sheaves carry the sheafified tensor product [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Let $\varphi:R\to T$ be a morphism of commutative ring objects [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], let $t$ be a global section of $R$, and let $I$ be a finite set. Use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and restriction of scalars [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Suppose global sections $b_i$ of $T$ give an $R$-module isomorphism
$$q:R^{\oplus I}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}T,\qquad (a_i)\longmapsto\sum_i\varphi(a_i)b_i.$$
Let $j_R:R\to A$ and $j_T:T\to B$ be morphisms of commutative ring objects exhibiting localization at $t$ and $\varphi(t)$, respectively. Explicitly, $j_R(t)$ is invertible and every ring map $R\to D$ making $t$ invertible factors uniquely through $j_R$; impose the analogous condition on $j_T$ and $\varphi(t)$.

There is a unique ring map $\varphi_t:A\to B$ with $\varphi_tj_R=j_T\varphi$. There is an $A$-module isomorphism
$$q_t:A^{\oplus I}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi_t}B,\qquad (a_i)\longmapsto\sum_i\varphi_t(a_i)j_T(b_i).$$
It satisfies $q_tj_R^{\oplus I}=j_Tq$ and is the unique $A$-linear map satisfying this equation. No injectivity of $\varphi$ or nonzero-divisor hypothesis on $t$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0EMC (lemma-simple-invert) and 0EMD (lemma-simple-invert-module); prescribed finite-basis comparison and its canonical square, extracted from the inverting-ell sentence of the blueprint parent proof

proof.text: Work on sections, retaining the internal scalar action. A morphism out of a sheafified tensor product into a sheaf is exactly a morphism from the objectwise tensor presheaf; hence multiplication and module actions are compatible bilinear operations on sections, and their axioms and linearity are tested on these operations. For finite $I$, the tuple sheaf $U\mapsto R(U)^I$ is a sheaf by componentwise gluing; its injections and projections satisfy the biproduct identities, so it realizes $R^{\oplus I}$. Thus $q$ gives, on every object, an $R(U)$-linear bijection $R(U)^I\to T(U)$. Denote its inverse coordinates by $c_i:T(U)\to R(U)$. They commute with restriction and satisfy $u=\sum_i\varphi(c_i(u))b_i$ and $c_i(\sum_j\varphi(r_j)b_j)=r_i$.

source.place: Tag 0EMC, lemma-simple-invert; agent-written finite-coordinate argument using the localization model and Sites Tags 00WB/00WK.

proof.text: The composite $j_T\varphi:R\to B$ sends $t$ to the invertible section $j_T(\varphi(t))$. The assumed universal property of $j_R$ therefore gives a unique ring map $\varphi_t:A\to B$ with $\varphi_tj_R=j_T\varphi$. Put $s=j_R(t)$ and $v=j_T(\varphi(t))$; then $\varphi_t(s)=v$, including the corresponding identity for their inverses.

source.place: Tag 0EMC, lemma-simple-invert; agent-written finite-coordinate argument using the localization model and Sites Tags 00WB/00WK.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-ring-localization-sheafification] to $(R,t,j_R)$ and $(T,\varphi(t),j_T)$. The resulting ring sheafifications are also underlying-set sheafifications by [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] shows that every section of $A$ is locally $j_R(r)s^{-n}$, and every section of $B$ is locally $j_T(u)v^{-n}$. Moreover, equality of two such fractions implies, after a further covering, equality of their presheaf fractions; the relation in the localization-model statement then gives $t^k(t^m r-t^n r')=0$ in $R$, respectively $\varphi(t)^k(\varphi(t)^m u-\varphi(t)^n u')=0$ in $T$. Exponents and numerators may vary with the member of the cover. These are local statements only; section rings of $A$ and $B$ are not asserted to be sectionwise localizations.

source.place: Tag 0EMC, lemma-simple-invert; agent-written finite-coordinate argument using the localization model and Sites Tags 00WB/00WK.

proof.text: On every object define $Q((a_i))=\sum_i\varphi_t(a_i)j_T(b_i)$. Ring distributivity makes this additive, and $Q((aa_i))=\varphi_t(a)Q((a_i))$ makes it $A$-linear for precisely the restriction-of-scalars action in the conclusion. The formula commutes with all restrictions and so defines an internal $A$-linear map. The identity $\varphi_tj_R=j_T\varphi$ and preservation of finite sums give $Qj_R^{\oplus I}=j_Tq$.

source.place: Tag 0EMC, lemma-simple-invert; agent-written finite-coordinate argument using the localization model and Sites Tags 00WB/00WK.

proof.text:
For local surjectivity, write an arbitrary section $x$ of $B$ locally as $j_T(u)v^{-n}$, using step 3. Set $a_i=j_R(c_i(u))s^{-n}$ on that member of the cover. Then
$$Q((a_i))=v^{-n}j_T\!\left(\sum_i\varphi(c_i(u))b_i\right)=v^{-n}j_T(u)=x.$$
Thus every section has preimages locally; no global lifting through a sheafification map has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 0EMC, lemma-simple-invert; agent-written finite-coordinate argument using the localization model and Sites Tags 00WB/00WK.

proof.text: For injectivity, suppose $Q((a_i))=0$ over $U$. Applying step 3 to the finitely many $a_i$ and successively refining the covers, write them simultaneously as $a_i=j_R(r_i)s^{-N}$ on each member of a covering: replace each exponent $n_i$ by $N=\max_i n_i$ and its numerator by $t^{N-n_i}r_i$. If $I$ is empty take $N=0$. Put $u=\sum_i\varphi(r_i)b_i$. Then $j_T(u)v^{-N}=0$. By the equality assertion of step 3, after a further covering there is $k\geq0$ with $\varphi(t)^ku=0$. Apply $c_i$, which is $R$-linear, to obtain $t^kr_i=0$. Consequently $j_R(r_i)=s^{-k}j_R(t^kr_i)=0$, so every $a_i$ vanishes on that covering. The separatedness axiom for $A$ gives $a_i=0$ over $U$. Hence $Q$ is injective on sections over every object. Notice that the argument uses a killing power, not cancellation in $R$ or $T$.

source.place: Tag 0EMC, lemma-simple-invert; agent-written finite-coordinate argument using the localization model and Sites Tags 00WB/00WK.

proof.text: Given $x\in B(U)$, choose the local preimages supplied by step 5. On any object with two arrows into covering members over $U$, their restrictions have the same $Q$-image, so step 6 makes them equal. The sheaf axiom for the tuple sheaf glues them uniquely to a preimage over $U$. The unique preimage commutes with restriction; it respects addition and $A$-scalars because $Q$ does and is injective. Thus $Q$ is an isomorphism of internal $A$-modules; set $q_t=Q$.

source.place: Tag 0EMC, lemma-simple-invert; agent-written finite-coordinate argument using the localization model and Sites Tags 00WB/00WK.

proof.text: If $H:A^{\oplus I}\to\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi_t}B$ is another $A$-linear map with $Hj_R^{\oplus I}=j_Tq$, evaluate this equation on the standard vector $e_i$ with entry $1$ in position $i$. It gives $H(e_i)=j_T(b_i)=Q(e_i)$. Every local tuple is $\sum_i a_i e_i$, so $A$-linearity forces $H=Q$. For $I=\varnothing$ the domain is the zero module and this assertion is immediate. This proves the stipulated uniqueness as well as the canonical square.

source.place: Tag 0EMC, lemma-simple-invert; agent-written finite-coordinate argument using the localization model and Sites Tags 00WB/00WK.
